items.text:
"Why not just call 1-800-MEDICARE myself?" is a fair question, and the honest answer starts with: you can.

That line is a useful resource. It can answer questions about the program, explain how enrollment works and help you look up plans. For a simple situation, it may be all you need.

Where people sometimes want more is in the specifics. Which plans in your county include your cardiologist? What happens to your prescriptions if you switch? Is the plan you already have still the right one? And who do you call in February when a claim does not look right?

An independent agent can help with those, and with the follow-up after you enroll. Your premium is set by the plan and is not higher because you used an agent.

Use whichever route fits. If you want a second set of eyes, we are happy to be one.

Honorbrook Insurance. (571) 354-0146 honorbrook-insurance.com

We do not offer every plan available in your area. Any information we provide is limited to those plans we do offer in your area. Please contact Medicare.gov or 1-800-MEDICARE to get information on all of your options.
